prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you left the game at the start of the fourth quarter to beat traffic. Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts tie, leans into microphone*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Committee, I appear before you today voluntarily, with nothing to hide.

I want to state, unequivocally and for the record: I am not now, nor have I ever been, a member of the Beat-the-Traffic Party.

*shuffles papers*

The allegations against me are based on circumstantial evidence at best. Yes, I was observed standing near the exit tunnel at the end of the third quarter. But I submit to this Committee that I was stretching my legs. A man is entitled to stretch his legs in this country, or at least he was, the last time I checked the Constitution.

The Committee has produced a parking lot receipt timestamped 8:47 PM. I do not dispute the receipt. What I dispute is the *interpretation* of the receipt. I remained in my vehicle listening to the fourth quarter on the radio, which any reasonable person would agree constitutes watching the game *in spirit.*

*pauses, wipes brow*

Now, have I ever *associated* with known early-leavers? I will not deny that my brother-in-law Gary once left a playoff game at halftime "because the baby was fussy." I was young. Foolish. We all attended cookouts we regret.

But I will NOT name names. You can subpoena my group chat, you can dim my Bluetooth, but I will not hand this Committee the identities of the four gentlemen who left Section 214 with me — *ALLEGEDLY* — with me.

Senator, I have sat through rain delays. I have endured a 38-point blowout in November with a wet sock. I bought the $14 nachos, sir. THE FOURTEEN DOLLAR NACHOS. And this Committee dares to question my loyalty?

Have you no decency? At long last, have you left no decency in the stadium... to beat traffic?

*sips water defiantly*

I yield the remainder of my time.
